ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2.label: UBS Dictionary of Biblical Hebrew v0.9.2 exact definitions and glosses
ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2.declared_from: The entry's own structure, read across all 21,626 routes on 6,539 keys. In 21,626 of 21,626 rows the route is the whole definition, character for character: each route is one SDBH record, either one gloss ('to distribute') or one definition ('man; ◄ son of Heman; ► temple singer; time of king David'), and the provider gives a meaning several glosses by writing several routes. 7,659 routes carry no mark at all; 3,595 are a mark-free gloss of at most four words. A definition has a head and, in 7,674 routes, notes opened by ◄ (origin, context), ► (role, purpose) and ≈ (association); idioms are written 'literally: X; hence: = Y' (3,295 times). The closed set is 41 marks and 58,686 occurrences, agreeing with the inventory; every occurrence falls in exactly one of 128 shapes, 0 unexplained. 58 occurrences in 46 routes divide readings in meaning (a labeled second meaning, a gloss packing two renderings, a second form of a name, two interjections); none is separated (see separates_on).

meaning_depends_on_region.;: Yes, in what it divides, not in whether it divides readings: in the head it closes the definition proper or its label (10,460 occurrences); after a note marker it divides one note item from the next (5,539). It never occurs in a marker-free route, by that region's definition.
meaning_depends_on_region.,: Yes: only in a short marker-free route (no ; ◄ ► ≈ = :, every comma piece at most four words, 118 routes) can a comma pack renderings; in the head and notes of a definition (7,979 occurrences) and in longer marker-free routes it is prose.
meaning_depends_on_region.others: No: every other mark means the same in the head, the notes and a marker-free route.

regions.note: Region here is a part of the route's own text, since the route is always the whole definition: 'marker-free' (no ; ◄ ► ≈ = :), 'head' (before the first note marker at depth 0) and 'notes' (after it).

;.means: Divides the parts of one SDBH record, never two readings: the head from a note (before ◄ ► ≈), one note item from the next, an idiom's literal rendering from its meaning ('literally: ...; hence: = ...'), a hedge ('meaning unsure') from the tentative definition, a label from the definition, the head from a further clause. One record describes one lexical meaning. The one exception is a second meaning the provider labels 'or:', 'either:' or 'alternatively', which divides in meaning and is not separated.
;.divides_readings: in meaning, at 26 of 15,999 occurrences (semicolon.before_alternative_label 26); not separated
;.region_dependent: Yes, in what it divides, not in whether it divides readings: in the head it closes the definition proper or its label (10,460 occurrences); after a note marker it divides one note item from the next (5,539). It never occurs in a marker-free route, by that region's definition.
;.evidence: 8,312 of 15,999 stand immediately before ◄, ► or ≈; 3,295 before 'hence'/'therefore'; 2,762 between note items after a marker; 507 before a hedge ('possibly', 'probably'). 2,569 follow the head 'man' of a name entry ('man; ◄ son of Heman; ► temple singer; time of king David'), which today's card prints as four pills: 'man', '◄ son of Heman', '► temple singer', 'time of king David'. 25 of 15,999 occurrences have a piece on either side that the provider also writes as a route of its own on the same key.
;.falsifier: A ';' (not an alternative label) whose piece on either side the provider also writes as a route of its own on the same key, i.e. treats as a reading: 25 today (census: piece_also_a_route_on_the_key). In 24 of them the piece is the record's head, which the provider also writes as a separate gloss or a sister definition ('man', 'hill', 'terebinth', 'one of the city gates of Jerusalem'): the head is attested as a reading there, but the record still joins it to its notes. A ';' between two pieces that each read as a whole definition of a different meaning with no 'or:'/'either:'/'alternatively' label would also falsify it; the census found none it could name, and owner question 2 lists the 21 unlabeled 'or'/'either' clauses for reading.

Those divide in meaning and are not separated.

◄.means: Opens a note of origin and context inside one definition: whom the referent descends from or belongs to, where it is, what it is made of or caused by, what it is like ('son of', 'tribe of', 'territory of', 'made of', 'caused by', 'as if'). Never a reading of its own.

◄.falsifier: A piece opened by ◄ that the provider also writes as a route of its own on the same key: 1 today.

►.means: Opens a note of role, purpose and consequence inside one definition: what the referent did or was, what it is used for, what followed ('father of', 'king of', 'family head', 'used for', 'in order to', 'after exile'). Never a reading of its own.

=.means: Opens the definition proper after a label or literal rendering ('hence: = action by which...'), or, in a gloss or aside, gives what a phrase means ('father's house = family', '(= delay)'). Never between two readings.

ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2.precedence_note: Nothing separates, so precedence decides only which mark's scope governs where two meet: the italic code, quotes and parentheses first (nothing inside them is structure), then ';' (the parts of one record), then the note openers, then ':' and '=' (label and definition), then ',' and '!' inside one part, then '>' and '/' inside one phrase.

unbalanced_parentheses.rule: Nothing to refuse: nothing separates, so a damaged scope cannot mis-cut anything. The route ships whole with the orphan character where the provider left it. Today's engine holds such a sense back as damaged and prints nothing for it.

ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2.separates_on_why: Every route is one record of one meaning. The marks that divide in meaning do so in 46 of 21,626 routes, and in each a cut would either print a piece that leans on the other's words ('to be' from 'to be, become happy'), leave a shared head or note attached to one alternative ('meaning unknown; possibly: = musical term' | 'or: = musical instrument' | 'or: = melody; ≈ ...'), or contradict the owner's ruling that a comma in UBS does not mean different entries. The provider's own way of offering a second reading is a second route (3,595 mark-free glosses of at most four words). So nothing is separated until the owner rules on the open questions.
ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2.not_done_here: The head is never taken as the reading: 'man' is not printed for 'man; ◄ son of Heman; ...', and 'hence: = action by which ...' is not printed without its literal rendering. A note is never printed as a reading. A packed gloss is never completed ('to be happy' is not manufactured from 'to be, become happy'). All three would be derivations.

open_questions.question: A gloss route that packs two or three renderings with a comma (or two interjections with '!'): one reading or several?

reading_a.says: One reading: the provider wrote one gloss, and the owner ruled that a comma in UBS does not mean different entries (declared here).

reading_b.says: Several readings, separated where each piece stands alone ('pain' | 'trouble'; 'to go' | 'to arrive'), never where a piece leans on another's words ('to be, become happy'), which no separation can print without completing it.

open_questions.evidence: The provider's ordinary second gloss is a second route (3,595 mark-free glosses of at most four words); in 3 of 9 complete packed commas a piece is also written as its own route on the key ('to go, to arrive' beside 'to go' and 'to arrive').

reading_a.says: One reading: the record is one entry for an uncertain word; the head ('meaning unknown') and any trailing note belong to every alternative (declared here).

reading_b.says: One reading per alternative, cut at the ';' before 'or:'/'either:'/'alternatively'; the shared head stays on the first piece and a trailing note on the last.
